statement_record.book: A coproduct diagram for an object ⟨a,b⟩ of C×C is a universal arrow to the diagonal Δ: an object c with injections i : a→c, j : b→c such that every pair f : a→d, g : b→d factors through a unique h : c→d with h∘i = f, h∘j = g. The object c = a⊔b is unique up to isomorphism; ⟨f,g⟩ ↦ h is a bijection C(a,d)×C(b,d) ≅ C(a⊔b,d) natural in d, inverse h ↦ ⟨h∘i, h∘j⟩. Injections need not be injective.

statement_record.book: In Set the pushout of ⟨f,g⟩ always exists: the disjoint union b ⊔ c with f x and g x identified for each x ∈ a. A similar construction (with quotient topology) gives pushouts in Top, including adjunction spaces. Pushouts exist in Grp; if f and g are monic the pushout injections u, v are monic and the vertex is the amalgamated product of b and c.
